problem: The EQA baseline (Das et al. 2018) seems to barely use vision when answering, and earlier work only compared uni- vs multi-modal models; it is unclear how the model reacts to different kinds of visual perturbation.
motivation: Dataset biases (repetitive templated questions, skewed answer priors, poor rendering, visually similar homes) let a model answer from language. Knowing how much and what kind of visual information the QA module actually extracts is needed to judge whether EQA models truly reason about vision.
key_idea: Probe the EQA question-answering module by training/evaluating with removed or perturbed visual input (blind, random noise, shuffled/incongruent frames) and compare against language-only and full models.
insight: Language-only (Ø-L) has a better mean rank (3.685) than the full model (4.352), and the full model's kappa is near 0 (-0.005). This means the model mostly exploits label distributions and language priors. At test time, incongruent images (acc 0.266) and black images (0.246) hurt less than random noise (0.211, MR 6.899), so the model relies on coarse, low-level visual structure rather than fine-grained content.
method: Vis-L: the standard EQA QA module (LSTM question encoder + multi-task pre-trained CNN on the last N=5 frames, attention fusion, MLP over 35 answers), trained on the original data
Blind-L: trained and tested with all-zero image arrays (3x256x256) in place of frames
Ø-L: vision stream removed, trained on questions only
Eval-Shuffled: Vis-L tested with frames from another episode (question fields shuffled across episodes), so images are plausible but incongruent
Eval-Blind / Eval-Random: Vis-L tested with zero images or uniform random noise images
Metrics: accuracy, mean rank of the correct answer, Cohen's Kappa, broken down by question type (colour_room, colour, location)

setting.backbone: Das et al. 2018 EQA QA module: LSTM + multi-task CNN + attention MLP (trained from scratch, CNN pre-trained)
setting.training_data: EQA dataset (Matterport3D scenes rendered in Habitat), automatically generated questions; 50 epochs, best validation loss checkpoint
setting.observation: egocentric RGB 256x256, last 5 frames of the navigation path
setting.action_space: not applicable (only the QA module is analysed; navigation actions turn left/right, forward, stop are described)

numbers.backbone: EQA QA module (LSTM + multi-task CNN + attention)
numbers.extra: QA module only, evaluated on the last 5 frames of the navigation
numbers.evidence: Table 1: Overall Accuracy 0.38, Overall Mean Rank 4.352, Kappa -0.005

numbers.method: Blind-L (trained and tested with black images)
numbers.extra: zero images at train and test
trained on original data, tested with uniform random noise images

numbers_note: Accuracy is printed as 0-1 fractions. The EQA split is not stated explicitly, so 'val' is assumed. Table 2 also has Eval-Shuffled (acc 0.266, MR 5.145, Kappa 0.013) and Eval-Blind (acc 0.246, MR 5.508, Kappa 0.004), which are not listed as separate entries.
results: The full model has the best accuracy (0.38) but a kappa near 0, and the question-only model has a better mean rank (3.685 vs 4.352). Perturbing vision at test time lowers accuracy to 0.266 (shuffled), 0.246 (blind) and 0.211 (random noise), so the model picks up coarse visual structure but not fine-grained content.
limitations: Only the QA module is analysed, with navigation held fixed; only one baseline model is studied, and no pre-trained multimodal transformers
Dataset issues (poor rendering, questionable colour annotations, only 15 distinct location QA pairs in the evaluation set) confound the conclusions, and no statistical tests or seeds are reported
Baselines that would solve the task better are not offered; the paper only suggests future directions
